title: Don't Go It Alone: The Gentleman's Call to Brotherhood https://thewaysofagentleman.substack.com/p/dont-go-it-alone-the-gentlemans-call-to-brotherhood
author: The Ways of a Gentleman
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (thewaysofagentleman.substack.com), September 13, 2026
summary: This piece argues that male friendship has collapsed dramatically in a single generation — citing a rise from roughly 3% of men reporting no close friends in 1990 to 15% by 2021 — and frames this as a genuine danger rather than a minor social trend. Drawing on historical models from Masonic lodges to Benjamin Franklin's Junto Club (a weekly gathering for moral and philosophical discussion), the author argues brotherhood functions as a 'forge' that tempers character through mutual challenge and accountability, not merely companionship. The piece surveys five concrete venues where modern men can rebuild this kind of bond — fraternal organizations, sports teams, Bible study or church men's groups, military service, and informal arrangements like book clubs or recurring dinner groups — treating the specific venue as less important than the consistency and intentionality behind it. It closes with an explicit call to action rejecting the premise that isolation is compatible with mature manhood.
points: A cited statistic anchors the essay's urgency: the share of men reporting no close friends rose from roughly 3% in 1990 to 15% in a 2021 Psychology Today survey.
Brotherhood is framed as more than companionship — 'a forge where one's character is tempered' — using Benjamin Franklin's Junto Club as a historical model of structured mutual challenge.

Five concrete venues are proposed for rebuilding male friendship: fraternal organizations (Freemasons, Elks), sports teams and leagues, church/Bible study groups, military or veterans' groups, and informal arrangements like book clubs or recurring dinners.
The specific venue matters less than consistency and intention — 'the form matters less than the consistency and intention' — positioning any regular, deliberate gathering as legitimate brotherhood.
The piece closes with an explicit rejection of the premise that isolation is compatible with mature manhood: 'Don't believe the lie that manhood is best lived in isolation.'
quotes: Few things in life shape a man more profoundly than the bonds of brotherhood.
A 2021 survey from Psychology Today found that 15% of men say they have no close friends, a marked rise from approximately 3% in 1990.
Brotherhood is more than companionship. It's a forge where one's character is tempered. Proverbs reminds us, "As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
For a historical reference, consider Ben Franklin's Junto Club. It was a small circle of men who met weekly to discuss questions of morality, politics, and philosophy.
For centuries, the military has been the crucible of brotherhood. Few bonds are as enduring as those forged under the strain of shared mission and sacrifice.
Brotherhood is not confined to formal groups. Book clubs or a regular dinner group can serve as modern equivalents of Franklin's Junto.
Don't believe the lie that manhood is best lived in isolation. Our forefathers knew better, and so should we.
